links.outcome: Missed abnormal findings among CXRs the AI classified as normal (negative predictive value vs radiologists)
links.effect: NPV 99.92% (95% CI 99.92-99.93), PPV 5.06%, overall agreement with radiologists 72.90% across 1,309,443 CXRs
links.quote: The analysis of 1309,443 CXRs from 1309,431 patients (median age: 35 years; IQR [29-42]; 1030,071 males [78.7 %]) in this study revealed a Negative Predictive Value (NPV) of 99.92 % (95 % CI: 99.92, 99.93), Positive Predictive Value (PPV) of 5.06 % (95 % CI: 4.99, 5.13) and overall percent agreement of the AI with radiologists of 72.90 % (95 % CI: 72.82, 72.98).

unlisted_practices: Using AI to rule out normal chest X-rays in high-volume screening so radiologists can focus on abnormal cases
Survey of radiologists on implementation challenges and impact after AI integration

screen.reason: The study evaluates the real-world post-deployment diagnostic accuracy and user perceptions of an AI chest X-ray triage software (qXR) across visa screening centers, but it does not compare outcomes with and without a specific guardrail or deployment practice.
